data: China Astronaut Research and Training Centre
China's EVA suit — used by Zhai Zhigang on the country's first spacewalk during Shenzhou 7

Chinese rear-entry EVA suit with architectural similarities to the Soviet Orlan design. First flown on Shenzhou 7 in 2008 when Zhai Zhigang became the first Chinese taikonaut to spacewalk. Operates on the Tiangong space station's Wentian airlock. Name means "flying in heaven" — also the name of the Apsara dancers in Chinese mythology.
China's EVA suit — architecturally similar to the Orlan, first flown on Shenzhou 7 in 2008

Chinese rear-entry EVA suit with architectural similarities to the Soviet Orlan design. First flown on Shenzhou 7 in 2008 when Zhai Zhigang became the first Chinese taikonaut to spacewalk. Now in operational use on the Tiangong space station's Wentian airlock. The name means "flying heaven" — a reference to the celestial flying spirits (feitian) from Buddhist cave art at Dunhuang, depicted on the suit's arm badge.
